base_path.description: The one directory this assistant's file surface may reach. Every path in a call is relative to it and the boundary is checked twice, lexically and after canonicalisation. `./edit` carries the same string, so a mutation that repoints one repoints both.

description.purpose: Filesystem CRUD inside one boundary: read, write, list and stat under `params.base_path`, and nothing above it.
description.use_when: The `file` occupant of a tools hive, reached on hop.tool_name == 'file'. Point `params.base_path` at the directory this assistant may actually touch; the shipped default is the machine's scratch directory, which is a real reach and is written down rather than left to be discovered.
description.not_in_scope: No editing in place -- that is the `edit` occupant beside it, sharing the same boundary code and the same root. No path outside the root, ever: `..` and absolute paths are refused before anything is opened, and the check runs again after canonicalisation, so a symlink out is refused too. And NO `params.sandbox`: this cell does its own I/O rather than starting a runner, so a process sandbox has nothing to bound here -- the boundary IS `base_path`.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one tool_result turn. hop.operation names which of the four ops ran -- and `unknown` when the arguments did not parse far enough to say, which is why this hive's exit edge names that value too. hop.bytes on a payload, hop.encoding only when the payload is base64 rather than text.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: a tool_call turn whose text is JSON args {op, path, ...}.
examples: {"op":"read","path":"notes.md"} -> tool_result with the file's text, hop { operation: 'read', bytes: 412 }
{"op":"read","path":"../etc/passwd"} -> tool_result, hop { operation: 'read', error_code: 'path_outside_boundary' } -- an ordinary result on the ordinary lane
